_README: Hand judgement of all 37 citation-support flags from the two laser curricula
that measured 24/118 (20.3%) and 13/116 (11.2%). Not a sample: 37 is the whole
population of flags from those two runs, so there is no sampling question.
Regenerate the evidence with `python scripts/classify_dl_flags.py`; the row order
is the order the flags appear in evidence_mapping.jsonl and is stable.
The rule applied to every row, stated so a re-judge can disagree with it rather
than with a mood:
unsupported   - read the WHOLE stored abstract and the assertion that actually
carries this marker: the paper still does not state it.
artifact_tail - the load-bearing fact IS in the abstract, past character 1200,
which is where `_SUPPORT_ABSTRACT_CHARS` cuts the excerpt the
judge was given. The judge could not have found it.
artifact_unit - the extracted 'claim' merges several distinct assertions (a
multi-branch IF/THEN/BECAUSE decision tree, a bold pseudo-
heading boundary, or a bare procedural parameter list), so the
pair judged was never one sentence with its citation. The
assertion carrying THIS marker is supported.
unusable      - no abstract stored, or the stored text is not an abstract.
Where both artifacts apply, `also` names the second one. The verdict field holds
the mechanism that alone decides the flag.

verdicts.why: The umbrella review's CONCLUSIONS and CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE — 'remains limited and heterogeneous', 'adjunct with unproven clinical benefit' — are quoted almost verbatim by the claim and sit entirely in the 919 withheld characters. The judge saw only OBJECTIVES and METHODS.

Five IF/THEN/BECAUSE branches merged into one claim. The branch citing this paper — 0.005% methylene blue, 660 nm, 3 min pre-irradiation, 40 s, 4 J, 37.57-100% reduction, 5 deciduous teeth — is verbatim in the VISIBLE part of the abstract.
Same merged decision tree. Its branch — Genc Sen & Kaya, n=84 RCT, lower pain at 24 h and 48 h, less analgesic — is what this abstract reports.

'meta-analysis was only possible for UAI ... no statistically significant difference in healing after 12 months' and 'very low strength of evidence for diode laser' are both in the 1815 withheld characters.
'multivariate analysis found that the size of periapical lesions, preoperative pain level, and laser treatment protocol were the main factors' — verbatim, 2207 characters past the cut.

The claim describes a pre-registered SR/meta-analysis of 5 RCTs of laser phototherapy in retreatment. The cited paper is an in vitro 3D-printed isthmus-cleaning study. Wrong paper, whole abstract read.

'There was no evidence that use of low energy level laser therapy (LLLT) prevented postoperative pain (very low quality evidence)' sits 5000+ characters into a 6724-character Cochrane abstract. The judge saw the search strategy.

'The included studies displayed significant heterogeneity ... limiting the potential for meta-analysis' is the DISCUSSION, in the withheld tail. The claim's second half (no included study reported safety data) is an absence the abstract does not assert either way.

'no included study enrolled patients without prior chemo-mechanical preparation' is an inference from the review's inclusion criteria, not something it states. The relevant text was in the visible portion and the judge was right.

A bare Procedural Protocol parameter list — 'Set parameters: 50 mJ, 25 Hz, 1 W, 300 us' — with no proposition to verify. 50 mJ / 25 pps / 300 us are verbatim in the visible METHODS; the 1 W belongs to a different paper's protocol.
'administered over 4 sessions - on the treatment day, and after 24 h, 48 h and 96 h' — verbatim, in the withheld 879 characters.
Merged decision tree. The marker rides a branch about radiographic healing while this SR is about postoperative pain; the pair the judge got is the whole tree.
Same merged tree, same mechanism.

'no significant difference in radiographic healing at 12 months for ANY laser modality' over-generalises: the review could meta-analyse healing only for UAI, and reports no healing meta-analysis for lasers at all. Compare row 4, which states the same finding accurately and is a tail artifact.

One claim merges Meire's 'insufficient evidence' conclusion with McGillivray & Dutta's own LAI findings. This paper's half — diode LAI superior at 6-48 h (visible), PIPS no different from needle but better than sonic/ultrasonic (withheld tail) — is supported.
'Meta-analysis on ... two studies using diode laser irradiation showed no significant difference in the prevalence of pain after 7 days' — verbatim in the withheld tail.

Three bold pseudo-headings merged. The marker's own sub-point is the aPDT mechanism sentence — photosensitiser, visible light, singlet oxygen and ROS — which this narrative review states verbatim in its visible portion. The Swetha and Ayhan figures belong to other papers in the same blob.
'no evidence that using CBCT rather than radiography ... was advantageous for healing (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.47)' — the claim quotes the interval exactly. It is 4000+ characters past the cut.
Same withheld sentence as row 11.
A mechanism claim — diode lasers act on chromophores, no significant cavitation. This outcomes review says nothing about wavelengths or mechanisms anywhere in its 3015 characters.
'Nd:YAG laser canal irradiation (2)' — the count the claim rests on — is in the withheld RESULTS.
'1.55 +/-0.51 mm ... 1.95 +/-0.71 mm (p < 0.05)' — verbatim in the withheld RESULTS.
Day-1 LLLT best, day-7 combined best, day-14 no difference — the whole three-part claim is the withheld RESULTS paragraph.
'the Combined group using the least (0.53 +/- 0.74 tablets)' — verbatim in the withheld tail.
'Nd:YAG lasers penetrate dentinal tubules up to 1000 um' is nowhere in this narrative review's abstract, whole. The abstract names the laser families but reports no penetration depth.
'photobiomodulation was applied using a 650 nm diode laser ... (25 mW, continuous mode, 1.5 J dosage)' — verbatim, 1467 characters past the cut.

A seven-branch decision tree as one claim. Its branch — Er:YAG SWEEPS did not significantly reduce residual filling material, 32 studies — is the paper's own conclusion, half visible and half withheld.
Same seven-branch tree. Its branch is this case series' three-phase protocol, first phase verbatim visible.

The one flag in all 37 whose abstract fits inside the excerpt (1058 chars), and it is a pure claim-unit artifact: the branch citing it says the recommendation rests on a single case report, which is what this paper is.
Same withheld LLLT sentence as row 7.

A protocol step carrying a concentration — 'Irrigate with 5.25% NaOCl throughout shaping' — attached to a review that states no concentration anywhere. The adjunct-not-replacement half is fair; the number is not this paper's.
A cavitation / PIPS / SWEEPS mechanism claim cited to a biofilm-removal meta-analysis that mentions neither cavitation nor either technique in its whole 1607 characters.
Blob spanning three sub-points. The one citing this paper — HPL and PIPS produce greater apical debris extrusion — is its subject.
Same blob; its sub-point is the aPDT mechanism sentence this review states.
'no significant difference in the prevalence of pain after 7 days' for aPDT and diode laser — withheld RESULTS.
Its half of the blob is the Cochrane LLLT sentence, 5000+ characters past the cut.
Blob merging Coelho's aPDT trial (this paper, and its figures are the paper's own) with Abaza's smear-layer study.
